 DPWH warns contractor of penalties over bridge collapse
 JG Jeffrey G. Damicog · 18 November 2026 · 10:07 AM PHT · 1 MIN READ 
 Department of Public Works and Highways
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) on Wednesday warned that the contractor of a P512-million bridge project in Samar could face severe penalties if construction defects were found to have caused the collapse of two girders.
 The girders at the Gandara Parallel Bridge project collapsed Tuesday, Nov. 17, during the removal of a roller attachment.
 “The DPWH assures the public that the contractor will face severe penalties if technical assessments reveal that the collapse was due to defects in construction,” the agency said.
 Also read DICT secretary Tasks focus on cybersecurity, connectivity 
 Public Works Secretary Giovanni Lopez has ordered the deployment of a technical team to assess the damage and determine the necessary corrective measures.
 The department also said it would comply with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s directive to ensure the safety of workers at the construction site.
 According to the DPWH, the contractor reported that no workers were injured in the incident.
 The contractor also accepted full responsibility for the collapse and assured the department that the replacement of the damaged girders would be undertaken at no cost to the government.
